title: Responsible for one another (Shevuot 39a)
hookLine: all Israel are responsible for one another
last: MAKE A TEACHER, ACQUIRE A FRIEND.

lines: I WILL BE SURETY FOR HIM.
cards: Famine in Canaan, and the brothers have to go back to Egypt for grain. The ruler there has said: don't come back without your youngest brother, Benjamin. Their father Jacob refuses; he has already lost Joseph.
Then Judah steps forward and says, in the King James words, "I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him." Put him on me. If he doesn't come home, the blame is mine.
Later, in Egypt, Judah keeps that promise, offering to stay as a slave in Benjamin's place.

teach.h: AREV: THE ONE WHO STANDS BEHIND THE DEBT.
teach.b: Arevim. Guarantors. The singular is arev, the one who stands behind a debt: if the borrower can't pay, the arev pays.
First, Judah. Readers hear the same Hebrew word in his promise to Jacob: I will be his guarantor. He puts his own life behind his brother's.
Second, the Talmud. In tractate Shevuot, the rabbis read a hard verse from Leviticus about people stumbling over one another as they flee.

They hear it as people stumbling through one another's failings, and draw a principle: all Israel are guarantors, one for another. Kol Yisrael arevim zeh bazeh. When one person falls, the others aren't bystanders.
They co-signed. Third, rabbinic law uses this idea in a surprising place.
Someone who has already said certain blessings can still say them again for another person who can't, because that person's obligation is partly theirs. Your duty doesn't end at your own edge.
Fourth, the weight and the comfort. The weight: no one can shrug at a neighbor's trouble and call it none of their business.
The comfort: nobody in the community stands alone in front of the debt. The streams of this block disagree about a great deal, and a guarantor doesn't sign only for the borrowers they agree with.
Judah didn't choose the brother who was easiest to protect. He chose the one who was in danger.

how: Jewish communities cite kol Yisrael arevim zeh bazeh when organizing help for members in need and for Jews in other places, and in Jewish law it allows one person to say certain blessings on another's behalf.

o: guarantors, each standing behind the others
judges appointed to settle money disputes
debtors who owe the community a fixed tax

p: I will be surety for him

s: arevim means people who mind their own business
it means guarantors: each stands behind the others.
Judah offered to stay as a slave in Benjamin's place
he kept his promise to Jacob.
the principle only applies to people you agree with
a guarantor stands behind the whole community.

games.q: you're Judah. your father won't let Benjamin go to Egypt, and the family needs grain. what do you do?
o: go without Benjamin and hope for the best.
put yourself behind him: if he doesn't come home, the blame is yours.
let your father decide and stay out of it.
games.why: Judah says "I will be surety for him," and in Egypt he offers himself as a slave in Benjamin's place.

practice: Picture the people you call yours, and look for the one who is stumbling right now: a neighbor who's sick, a friend between jobs, a family that just lost someone, a newcomer nobody has spoken to yet.
Ask what you could put your own hand behind, a meal, a ride, an introduction, a phone call that isn't rushed, and pick the one you'd really do. If you pray, pray for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Arevim. Guarantors: all Israel stand behind one another, like co-signers on a debt, as the Talmud teaches in Shevuot. Today's word.
